subject: zoology_2
question_text: Name the different types of salivary glands of man and their locations in the human body.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.46, VSAQ 53. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Revised 2026-09-05: s1_pairs' why said the glands are named by where their ducts open, which is not so — each is named for where the gland lies — and its margin note no longer claims the word pairs is checked.

insider_note: Say three PAIRS, not three glands, and give a location for each.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The three pairs
steps.why: Each gland is named after the place where the gland itself lies — beside the ear, under the lower jaw, under the tongue — so the name and the location belong together.
common_mistakes: Writing three glands instead of three pairs. They are paired.
Naming the pancreas. It is not a salivary gland.
steps.memory_tip: Near the ear, under the jaw, under the tongue.
steps.margin_note: Say pairs, not glands. There are three pairs, six glands in all.
lines: There are 3 pairs of salivary glands in man:

steps.label: Their locations
steps.why: Saliva has to reach the food while it is being chewed, so all three open into the mouth cavity from close by.
common_mistakes: Placing the parotid under the tongue. It lies below the ear lobe.
Giving no location for one of the three.
steps.memory_tip: Par-otid sits by the ear, sub-lingual under the tongue.
steps.margin_note: One line each, in the same order.
